title: Unravel Lease Controller and Capacity Planner: Consolidate GPU lease logic, upgrade dependencies, and reduce termination latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Refactor and decouple the Lease Controller responsibilities from the Capacity Planner for the GPU fleet, eliminate duplicated lease reconciliation logic, upgrade key dependencies, and address termination path performance regressions. The goal is to reduce median node termination latency, fix goroutine leaks during aggressive scaling events, and make the planner component easier to unit test and reason about.
background: Over the past year several hotfixes grew the lease/heartbeat code path in two places: the lease-controller (responsible for node heartbeats and eviction decisions) and the capacity-planner (responsible for scheduling capacity deltas). Duplication led to inconsistent grace windows, subtle race conditions during rapid scale-up/scale-down, and leaked goroutines when nodes transitioned between states. Recent incidents (incident-2025-11-gpu-surge) exposed a 30s tail termination spike. We want a single canonical lease reconciliation surface, clearer ownership boundaries, and a dependency bump to client-go and cloud SDKs to get bugfixes and improved informer behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Lease reconciliation lives in a single package with a well-defined interface consumed by the planner and node manager
Unit tests covering lease acquisition, renewal, and graceful eviction triggers with simulated clock
Client-go upgraded to v0.27.x and cloud-provider-gpu bumped to v3.4.1 with changelog references
End-to-end benchmark showing >=15% reduction in median termination latency and elimination of goroutine leaks under load
Canary rollout plan documented and console dashboard with lease/eviction metrics added
work_items: Extract LeaseManager interface and implementation from capacity-planner into pkg/leasecontroller
Remove duplicate heartbeat loop in planner and replace with LeaseManager.Subscribe() primitive
Add simulated clock to tests to deterministically test grace windows and timeouts
Upgrade client-go to v0.27.x and reconcile informer usage changes
Bump cloud-provider-gpu and nvidia-driver-sdk to latest minor fixes
Run 4-stage canary: unit tests -> integration cluster -> canary fleet (10% capacity) -> full rollout
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Spike completed — prototyped LeaseManager with Subscribe/Notify model, verified unit testability.
2026-02-25: Decided to keep Lease acquisition atomic and expose only Subscribe() and ForceRenew() to consumers — reduces coupling to underlying informer implementation.
2026-03-02: Opened infra PR to upgrade client-go to v0.27.3; required small changes to informer factory initialization. See PR #4213.
2026-03-05: First end-to-end integration run showed median termination latency down 12% but tail still present. Identified remaining tail due to blocked goroutine in drain watcher.
2026-03-10: Fixed goroutine leak in drain watcher by adding context cancellation propagation. Integration run shows goroutine count stable across scale tests.
2026-03-12: Planner replaced heartbeat loop with LeaseManager.Subscribe(); merging serving PR after 2 approvals. Preparing canary baseline metrics collection.
review_feedback: PM review (Sana Li): Ensure console exposes per-customer lease failures; added as follow-up label.
Design review (Ishaan Gupta): Suggested shades of state in dashboards to indicate transient vs terminal evictions.
Security review (Olivia Chen): No secrets exposure from dependency bump; recommended runtime test for RBAC changes.
risks: Dependency upgrade may change informer semantics and increase reconciliation events temporarily
Canary failure mode must gracefully fallback to previous planner; a rollback plan is required
Changes to eviction timing could surface customer-visible shorter grace windows if misconfigured
mitigations: Keep old heartbeat behavior behind feature flag until canary completes
Add automated rollback job that restores previous image and waits for health checks
Expose grace window as a runtime config with a safe default and per-tenant override
